senses.gloss:
Āyu appears in the Rigveda with kutsa and atithigva as having been defeated, with Indra's aid, by tūrvayāṇa, who is believed by Pischel to have been King of the Pakthas. Possibly he is elsewhere referred to as victorious, by Indra's aid, over veśa. Elsewhere he is quite mythical.
Foot notes i. 53, 10; ii. 14, 7; vi. 18, 3; viii. 53, 2; Bergaigne, Religion Védique, 1, 60.
Vedische Studien, 1, 71-75.
Rv. x. 49, 5; but the word is possibly not a proper name.
Cf. Macdonell, Vedic Mythology, 100, 135, 140.
